Use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a) to find the solutions.

To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine whether each stationary point is a maximum, minimum, or saddle point, find the second derivative, f''(x), and evaluate it at each stationary point. If f''(x) is positive, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) is negative, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) is zero, the test is inconclusive.
